#2941. Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

(See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.)

Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout quickly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

Zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:

This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

From here, it's all about the follow through.  We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

#2935. Here’s How Many Shares of Procter & Gamble You’d Need to Own to Collect $1,000 in Annual Dividends

Shoppers are watching every dollar they spend, yet Procter & Gamble keeps growing its revenues and has raised its dividend for 70 straight years.

By John Ballard – Nov 26, 2026 at 3:09PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Procter & Gamble ›

Procter & Gamble (PG +0.44%), the company behind brands like Tide, Pampers, Gillette, Charmin, and Crest, pays a quarterly dividend of $1.0885 per share. That works out to roughly $4.35 per share each year. To collect $1,000 a year, you would need about 230 shares, which would cost just over $39,800 at the stock's Nov. 25 closing price of $173.23. That's income from household products that people use every day.

In this difficult economy, shoppers are watching every dollar they spend, yet Procter & Gamble is still growing. Organic sales (a metric that excludes the impacts of foreign currency swings and recent acquisitions) rose 4% year over year last quarter, mostly because people bought more of its products.

Management maintained its full-year outlook, even as it sees rising costs for materials, energy, and shipping. That matters because people keep buying laundry detergent, diapers, and toothpaste even when they cut back elsewhere. P&G has also raised its dividend for 70 consecutive years, making it one of the rare Dividend Kings — companies that have raised their payouts for 50 straight years or more.

The main risk P&G faces now is cost pressure. If higher costs persist, the company's profits could flatten out, leaving less room for future dividend increases. P&G can offset some of this pressure through its scale, which gives it bargaining power with suppliers and retailers, and through its cost-cutting programs.

The stock trades at about 25 times this fiscal year's earnings estimates, and analysts expect earnings to grow about 4.7% annually. That's not a bargain valuation, but it's a reasonable price for a business that keeps growing and returning a growing cash payout to shareholders year after year. For investors, P&G remains a solid stock to hold for long-term dividend income.

#2934. LeBron triple-double, Maxey 30-piece lead Sixers over Heat

The Philadelphia 76ers got back in the win column on Wednesday evening, taking down the visiting Miami Heat 111-104 in NBA Cup group play.

Joel Embiid was ruled out for this one after having been doubtful on the injury report since yesterday because of illness. This was the second game in a row Embiid missed due to being sick.

The Sixers were led by tremendous nights from LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey. James, who notched his first triple-double as a Sixer, put up 25 points on 9-for-15 field goal and 4-for-6 three-point shooting with 12 assists, 10 rebounds and a steal. Maxey added 30 points shooting 12-for-21 from the floor. VJ Edgecombe came alive in the second half to chip in 18 points.

The bad news is that Jaylen Brown exited the game just before halftime after seemingly favoring and grabbing at his hamstring. He was quickly ruled out for the rest of the contest with hamstring tightness. Something to be aware of going forward, for sure.

The good news is that the Sixers are now 15-4 and have off tomorrow. They're back in action Friday.

It didn't take long to see how Miami benefits from being third in the association in pace. In the first three minutes, the Heat got out ahead in transition three separate times for easy buckets before the Sixers defense even made it back up the other end. The Sixers aren't that slow, but the Heat were running circles around them early.

Jabari Walker got his third start tonight in Joel Embiid's absence, and it went right to work doing the little things right. He buried a second-chance triple off a LeBron James offensive rebound then got down the defensive end to draw an offensive foul out of Giannis. Jabari had seven points on 3-for-3 field goal shooting in his first six minutes on the floor.

If you read any of the Bell Ringers I usually write, you know I cannot stop talking about LeBron's passing. Well, I'm here to talk about it again. It's not just one pass. It's every single pass he makes. He waits until the exact millisecond to release perfectly targeted passes that set up the Sixers for sometimes wide open buckets.

Tyrese Maxey led the way for the Sixers' scoring in the first quarter with 13 points on 5-for-8 field goal, 1-for-2 three-point shooting. The consistent contribution of points helped steady the Sixers' offense after starting off the game a bit disjointed. Philly trailed Miami by three points after one.

LeBron has this tendency to just absolutely lock in offensively in insane bursts. He goes from the main facilitator to a mode of "hold on y'all, I got this myself" and, in year 24, he's absolutely still got it. James had the ball in his hands for three straight Sixers' possessions and turned each into three points — one and-1, and two threes. He wasn't done. A minute later, he pulled up again from not far over midcourt for the ultimate heat check. Three more points. It ended up being a 14-3 Sixers run that gave them the lead, courtesy of LeBron James, single-handed.

It's been a very quiet night so far from Jaylen Brown. With just four minutes left in the half, Brown has two points on 1-for-6 field goal shooting with not much else to show for himself on the stat sheet. He hasn't made a ton of mistakes, necessarily, but more so has been relatively inconsequential so far and can't seem to get a shot to fall. A far cry from last game, his return from a hamstring strain, where he looked as solid as ever.

Just a quick note (and, yes, I admit in saying this I am incredibly biased)… Giannis gets a VERY friendly whistle. I get it, he's a superstar. But compare the amount of contact he takes that is getting called a foul versus the amount of contact Tyrese Maxey takes with no whistles.

The Sixers — especially considering the absence of Joel Embiid — are doing a great job so far containing Bam Adebayo. At halftime, Adebayo had just five points on 2-for-8 field goal shooting

The Sixers ended the half on a 7-0 run to help them to a 62-53 lead going into the break. That's the good news. That bad news is that Brown left the half a few seconds early after seemingly favoring his left leg and grabbing at his hamstring. He went straight back to the locker room.

The team was quick to rule out Brown for the rest of the game due to hamstring tightness. Dean Wade started the second half in his spot.

Philadelphia has had a tendency to come out of halftime looking a bit sluggish or out of sorts… not tonight. The Sixers ripped off a quick 7-0 run just a minute or so into the second half to push their lead to double-digits. It was the usual suspects, James and Maxey, chipping in with the addition of VJ Edgecombe getting involved.

Edgecombe had a relatively quiet first half, but he seemed energized to come out for the second. The sophomore assisted the Sixers' first two buckets of the third frame and then scored the next two himself. He added a triple and a steal a few minutes later. That's one thing that Edgecombe seems to possess beyond his years: patience. It doesn't matter how few opportunities he gets early on in a game, he never gets discouraged and is always ready whenever he is called upon.

It's a different game entirely when the Sixers are actually hitting their three-pointers. With just a few minutes left in the third, six Sixers have sank at least one three-pointer and three players have multiple. They're shooting 45.8% from long range and it certainly makes holding on to a narrow lead just a bit easier.

It's been very nice to have Dominick Barlow back. In just his third game of the season after making his debut this past Saturday, Barlow continued putting in some really serviceable minutes at the backup center position featuring solid rim protection, grabbing offensive boards, putting back buckets and setting some big screens. He and Walker have been a decent one-two punch at the center position without Embiid available tonight.

The Sixers brought a nine-point lead into the final frame. Their lead was quickly extended back into the double-digits with two back-to-back triples from Anfernee Simons — his first two field goals of the night, making him the seventh Sixer to knock down a three-pointer in this one.

Apologies for the redundancy but the Lebron passes just get more and more ridiculous. It is just beyond anything I've ever seen done so well night in and night out, every single game. Here's an absurdly accurate lob to Edgecombe from half court to extend the Sixers lead to 14.

Edgecombe has absolutely come alive since halftime. From all the statistical contributions to just the extra effort plays that won't show on the sheet, he has his handprints all over this second half and was a big factor in the Sixers holding on to this lead.

#2933. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the company's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

Buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.  Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

This prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

#2931. NBA Cup 2026: 76ers' LeBron James oldest to post triple-double; Rockets' Kevin Durant fifth ever to score 33,000 points

Early in the second quarter Wednesday night in NBA Cup group play, LeBron James pulled up from Broad Street.

He drilled a 35-foot 3-pointer amid a torrid stretch that saw him make a trio of triples and score 14 straight points for the 76ers on Thanksgiving Eve. Before that sequence, the Sixers were trailing the Miami Heat by three points at Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena. Afterward, they were up eight.

While becoming the oldest player in NBA history to notch a triple double — at 41 years and 330 days old — James continued his recent hot streak from beyond the arc, going 4 of 6 on 3-point attempts. Philadelphia shot 14 of 35 from long range en route to a 111-104 victory.

The Heat (10-7) would have clinched East Group B had they come out on top, but Philadelphia (15-4) denied Miami an eighth consecutive win, despite losing Jaylen Brown to a hamstring injury late in the first half and Joel Embiid being sidelined by illness.

Nick Nurse's squad is now 2-1 in NBA Cup competition; Erik Spoelstra's Heat dropped to that same mark.

James finished with a season-high 25 points and 12 assists, plus 10 rebounds, with maybe his most notable dime taking place early in the fourth quarter. The 22-time All-Star showed his elite court vision, timing a halfcourt lob perfectly to connect with VJ Edgecombe for a layup. James later dialed up an alley-oop for forward Dominick Barlow to throw down.

Edgecombe was among the Sixers players stepping up in the absence of Brown and Embiid, as Philadelphia protected its nine-point halftime lead and kept Miami at arm's length over the final two quarters. He had 18 points, and Tyrese Maxey poured in 30.

The Heat, who wound up trailing by 16 late in the final frame, were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, who clocked out with 32 points, 14 rebounds and 4 assists.

Kevin Durant is now one of five NBA players to score 33,000 points. The 38-year-old Houston Rockets forward achieved that feat on Wednesday night in a 116-104 home victory against the Phoenix Suns. He joined James, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant.

Durant did so while piling up 20 points for Houston (14-5), which, despite already being eliminated from NBA Cup knockout-round contention, kept pace in the upper echelon of the Western Conference standings.

The Rockets improved to 2-2 in Cup group play, while the Suns (9-8) slid to 1-2. They, too, have been eliminated from knockout-round contention in West Group A.

Along the way, Houston center Alperen Şengün passed Hakeem Olajuwon for the second-most triple-doubles in franchise history. Şengün, only 24 years old, secured his 15th performance of that kind with 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists.

Late in the game, Suns wing Dillon Brooks got into it with Durant and was ejected after receiving his second technical foul of the night.

Although the Minnesota Timberwolves lost LaMelo Ball to an ankle injury Wednesday, they held on to defeat the Oklahoma City Thunder 113-106.

Jaden McDaniels came through, big time, in the West Group B matchup. In fact, by game's end, he was the third player in Wolves history to log at least 30 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists in consecutive games. That elite company also includes Karl-Anthony Towns and Kevin Garnett.

After going for 34 points, 10 rebounds and 6 assists on Monday in a win over the Brooklyn Nets, McDaniels put up 32 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists this time out versus the Thunder (10-9), who are 2-7 in their last nine games and eliminated from Cup knockout-round contention.

Minnesota (14-5), on the other hand, is atop West Group B with a 3-0 record. McDaniels beat the third-quarter buzzer with a ridiculous off-balance shot. A late 3-pointer from Wolves guard Ayo Dosunmu helped seal the deal.

Note: "E —" denotes teams that have been eliminated from knockout round contention, whereas "Y —" denotes teams that have clinched their NBA Cup division.

For Thanksgiving, here is, if not a feast, at least an appetizer of NBA trade rumors as we move toward the end of the month.

The answer depends on who you ask. As league sources from other teams have told NBC Sports, they expect Washington to at least entertain offers from other teams — the Wizards need to build long-term around AJ Dybantsa and Davis would bring back a haul (while Trae Young has the most untradable contract in the league right now.

However, it's no lock Davis will end up on the market, reports Jake Fischer of The Stein Line. Davis isn't pushing for it, he's playing at a high level, and if the Wizards look like a playoff team they may not be looking to deal, even though he can be a free agent next summer (Davis has a $62.8 million player option and has said he doesn't want to talk extension during the season). If Davis becomes available, keep an eye on the Toronto Raptors, Golden State Warriors and Atlanta Hawks, Fischer adds.

Maybe this is all posturing by the Wizards. Either way, what is clear is that this conversation is happening close to the trade deadline, not before.

While the parents are away — owner Steve Ballmer and head of basketball operations Lawrence Frank are suspended — GM Trent Redden will play.

Multiple reports say the Clippers are expected to be sellers at the deadline, most recently from Jake Fischer of The Stein Line. LA is willing to move their deep group of veterans — pay particular attention to center Brook Lopez and wing Derrick Jones Jr., who are on expiring deals — to get back picks and young players to pair with the backcourt they like of Darius Garland and rookie Keaton Wagler. Only fitting for LeBron James to have his best game as a Sixer against the Miami Heat.

The King looked like the Heatles version Wednesday, securing his first triple-double of the season as the Sixers took down Miami 111-104 (full recap here). The win keeps the team's NBA Cup chances alive as they continue group play Friday night against the Indiana Pacers.

This was also a rare non-clutch win for the Sixers, who basically led from the second quarter on. James and Tyrese Maxey carried the offense for much of the night, while VJ Edgecombe filled in the gaps. With Joel Embiid out of the lineup because of an illness, the trio of Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Adem Bona all made an impact.

The only bad news from the night was Jaylen Brown being forced to leave the game at the end of the first half. The team ruled him out for the second half with left hamstring tightness, an injury that forced him to miss two games last week.

(Happy Thanksgiving to all who celebrate! We're all thankful for all of you!)

LeBron James: 25 points, 12 assists, 10 rebounds, , 4-of-6 3PT, 1 steal

LeBron was sensational Wednesday night. His second-quarter heater, which saw him bury three triples — including a heat check from the parking lot — helped put the Sixers in front. They really controlled the game from there.

The threes definitely helped, but it was a vintage James performance. He bullied his way to the rim. He found open teammates with gorgeous passes. He pulled down tough rebounds.

While the LeBron pass was ridiculous, don't sleep on the Edgecombe finish here.

The Center Triumvirate (Walker, Barlow, Bona): 16 points, 16 rebounds, 3 blocks, 1 steal

Piecing together 48 minutes without Embiid has generally felt like an impossible task. This season, it's felt even more difficult.

Against a frontcourt featuring Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, the trio of Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Adem Bona did a sensational job.

Antetokounmpo is great and he's going to get his, but those three (and Dean Wade) made him work for everything. Adebayo had a tough night, going just 6-of-16 from the field.

Barlow in particular has been outstanding since coming back from his back injury. Since making his season debut last Saturday against the Milwaukee Bucks, Barlow has been incredibly impactful offensively, defensively and on the glass.

#2920. SpaceX Is a Great Company. Is It a Great Stock at This Price?

SpaceX's current stock price leaves no room for error.

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 3:36PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›

Warren Buffett, perhaps the greatest investor of all time, once said: "It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price." However, even a wonderful company isn't worth buying at just any price. Earning outstanding long-term returns requires investors to buy stocks at the right price. On that note, let's consider one popular company on the market right now: Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%). The company arguably boasts a very strong business, but is its current stock price fair?

SpaceX is a leader in rocket technology. It helped pioneer reusable rockets and became the leader in space launch, contracting a significant amount of business from various U.S. government agencies. The company has also become a leader in satellite-based connectivity. Its constellation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites is far larger than that of any competitor.

In addition, SpaceX offers various artificial intelligence (AI) services, including access to its Grok large language model and compute capacity through a network of data centers. It isn't just the breadth of SpaceX's business that makes it a great company. It has arguably built a robust competitive advantage. Consider the company's space launch business.

Building rockets is capital-intensive, but that's just step one. They then have to go through multiple stages of testing before they can fly regularly. That's not to mention the expensive and time-consuming process of obtaining the necessary regulatory approvals that allow companies to legally fly rockets. SpaceX has already gone through all that with its Falcon 9, a partially reusable vehicle that has helped significantly slash space launch costs.

It has also made tremendous progress with its next-gen rocket, Starship, which has now undergone more than a dozen flight tests. SpaceX's rocket technology is superior to that of its competitors. That's why it is the market leader by far. Given the financial and regulatory barriers to entry, not to mention the time it takes to develop and build rockets, the company has a strong competitive edge. There is something similar going on with SpaceX's connectivity business.

Launching satellites into orbit takes time, a lot of money, and the appropriate authorizations. Also, service quality generally improves as the number of satellites increases. That's why it won't be easy for competitors to catch up to SpaceX here. Further, the company's financial results have been improving. In the third quarter, SpaceX recorded $14.6 billion in revenue, up 161% year over year.

The company's Super Intelligence segment -- through which it offers various AI services -- posted $7.6 billion in revenue, up 830% year over year. Connectivity revenue was $5.2 billion, 69.5% higher than the year-ago period.

And space revenue was $1.8 billion, up 6% year over year. On the bottom line, SpaceX recorded a net income of $4.4 billion, versus a net loss of $1.1 billion in the prior-year quarter. SpaceX's improving financials, strong lead and competitive moat across two of its business segments, and fast-growing AI business make it a robust company.

Now for the second question: Is SpaceX attractive at its current price? Shares are trading at about $126 as of writing, and its market cap is $1.7 trillion. Based on its trailing 12-month revenue of $32.04 billion, the stock is trading at about 53x sales. That's very high, but the company deserves a premium, given the strength of the business and how fast it is growing.

Also, it's perhaps more telling to look at the forward-looking earnings multiple. SpaceX's current forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, based on expected earnings over the next 12 months, is 44.2 -- that, again, looks high, and we have to factor in some uncertainty with the company's prospects. SpaceX is significantly exposed to regulatory risks across all three of its businesses.

Also, its fastest-growing segment, SI, which now accounts for more than half of its top line, is the unit where its moat is arguably less established. The SI business also risks a significant slowdown, which would reduce year-over-year revenue growth and margins, given how much SpaceX is spending on its AI build-out.

With all that said, I'd consider buying SpaceX at roughly 30x forward earnings -- that may undermine its prospects somewhat, but it would also give me a relatively healthy margin of error. But that means that at its current 44.2x forward earnings, the stock is too expensive, at least for me. I'd wait for a steeper decline to initiate a position.
